held.title: Links to published documents without a listed Markdown extension stop resolving
held.body:
The new check skips any target whose extension is not one of `.md .markdown .mdown .mkd .mkdn .mdwn`, and it runs before the metadata is read. Before this change, mark resolved any text file that carried mark metadata.

This hits two kinds of file:
- Documents published from files with other extensions, such as `.mdx`, `.qmd`, `.Rmd` or `.txt`, passed to mark via `--files`.
- Files whose names contain a dot but have no real extension, such as `release-1.2` or `.notes`. `filepath.Ext` returns `.2` or `.notes` for these.

A link to such a document now stays as a relative file path, so it is broken on the Confluence page. Nothing reports it, not even `--check-links`, because the skip is silent.

I could not check whether mark supports publishing files with non-`.md` extensions. If it does, a fix would be to keep the cheap skip only for files with no mark metadata. For example: read the headers with title derivation turned off (`TitleFromFilename`/`TitleFromH1` false), and look up only files that are Markdown or declare an explicit `Title`/`Space`.
